content.what_it_is: Python (numpy/matplotlib) port of plot_wave_vessel_island.m for the FUNWAVE-TVD vessel_island_beach case: instead of writing a movie it saves one PNG per snapshot in the user-supplied range. It sets fdir/fdep from relative-looking os.path.join('Users','Gaby',...) paths (L10-L11), loads eta_00001 into an unused variable mask (L13-L14), asks for start/end frame numbers ns/ne via input() (L17-L18), loads depth.txt as dep1 for grid sizing (L20, L22), and builds coordinates from x0=0.0, y0=2.0, dx=1.0 with y also using dx (L24-L29). Per frame num in range(ns,ne) (L35): creates a numbered 8x6-inch, 200-dpi figure (L37), loads eta_<fnum> (L38-L40), masks eta>10.0 via np.ma.masked_where (L42), draws pcolor with coolwarm, colorbar labeled eta (m), clim(-0.5,0.5) (L44-L47), labels Y/X, tight axes (L49-L51), titles 'Time = <(num-1)*2.5> sec' with the value zero-padded by '%.4d' (L53-L56), and saves fig_eta_<num>.png (L58-L61).
entities: script (no function/class definitions; top-level Python script)
mask — array loaded from eta_00001, never used (L14)
y — y coordinate array, using dx (L29)
NUM — num-1 for the time label (L53)

equations.ref: masking dry/land sentinel values above 10 m
time label assuming 2.5 s output interval

io.name: per-frame pcolor of masked eta with colorbar

verbatim_spans.text: eta_masked = np.ma.masked_where(eta>10.0,eta) # do nt plot where eta>10. 0

unresolved: fdep+'depth.txt' (L20) concatenates without a path separator, producing '.../vessel_island_beachdepth.txt' — a path bug; os.path.join is used everywhere else.

The os.path.join('Users','Gaby',...) paths (L10-L11) are relative (no leading separator), so they resolve under the current working directory rather than the absolute /Users/Gaby intended by the comment at L8.

dx=1.0 here (L26) versus dx=2.0 in the MATLAB sibling and mk_depth (dx=2.0); y0=2.0 (L25) also differs from the MATLAB y0=0.0 — coordinate axes will disagree with the depth grid actually generated by mk_depth.

'%.4d' applied to NUM*2.5 (L54) formats a float with an integer conversion; in Python 3 this raises no error only for whole floats via %d truncation semantics ('%.4d' % 2.5 actually raises TypeError in Python 3 for floats — script likely written for Python 2).
range(ns,ne) (L35) excludes ne, unlike the MATLAB ns:ne inclusive loop.
mask (L14) is loaded but never used.
The 2.5 s output interval implied by the title (L54) is unverifiable from this file.
